headline: AI capex hangover and frontier defaults leave a slower, poorer, more walled-off world

events: US tariff regime extended and broadened to pharmaceuticals and chips via Section 232; EU and China retaliate selectively, keeping average US tariff near 17%
Fed trims to ~3.25% amid sticky 3% inflation; ECB holds at 2%; BoJ inches to 1%
Ukraine front freezes into an armed ceasefire without settlement; reconstruction financing stalls over frozen-asset disputes
Hyperscaler AI capex passes $600bn a year; enterprise adoption rises to ~16% of firms but measured productivity gains stay modest
Two frontier economies (one in West Africa, one in South America) miss Eurobond payments and enter G20 Common Framework talks
Contested US election produces divided government; debt-ceiling brinkmanship briefly pushes 10-year Treasury yields above 5.2%
China's growth slips to ~3.5% as property deflation lingers; Beijing exports overcapacity in EVs and steel, triggering new EU and Mexican anti-dumping duties
Oil spikes to ~$105 for two months after Strait of Hormuz harassment incidents, lifting G20 inflation to a 3.6% peak
Pakistan secures its 26th IMF programme after a near-default; Egypt rolls debt via Gulf deposits
COP33 ends with weak NDC updates; global emissions flat-to-slightly up
AI capex correction: two large model labs restructure and data-centre orders are cut 25%; Nasdaq falls ~30% peak-to-trough and US enters a shallow recession
Global unemployment peaks at 5.6% as white-collar hiring freezes compound AI-driven back-office cuts in call centres, BPO hubs and junior professional roles
Fed cuts back to 2.25%; fiscal deficits widen across the G7 with no consolidation plan
Kenya and a large frontier Asian borrower restructure external debt; Sri Lanka-style protests in several capitals
Border clashes between Ethiopia and Eritrea escalate into an interstate war drawing in Gulf patrons
Recovery is sluggish (~2.5% world growth); cheaper compute after the bust accelerates mid-sized-firm AI adoption
Japan's 30-year JGB yield breaches 4%, forcing a BoJ yield cap on the long end and a quiet return to financial repression
EU agrees a modest joint defence-borrowing facility but fails on capital-markets union; France downgraded to A+
Renewables hit ~40% of global electricity on Chinese solar and batteries, yet coal use in India and Southeast Asia stays elevated
Housing protests and populist gains in Spain, Canada and Australia; rent controls spread
Warming reaches ~1.57C on a multi-year average; a record South Asian heatwave cuts wheat output and prompts Indian export bans
US debt reaches ~132% of GDP; interest costs exceed defence spending; Treasury expands bill issuance and Fed quietly tolerates 3%+ inflation
WTO dispute settlement still defunct; a de facto three-bloc trade system (US-aligned, China-centred, non-aligned 'swing' hub of India/Gulf/ASEAN) solidifies
About 31% of firms use AI in production; cumulative displacement reaches ~38m jobs, partly offset by new roles but with wage polarisation
IMF quota reform again deferred; Global South borrowers increasingly turn to Chinese and Gulf bilateral lenders

winners: Gulf states and India as non-aligned trade and capital hubs
Chinese clean-tech exporters selling into the Global South
Defence contractors and owners of grid, power and land assets
losers: Frontier-market debtors in Africa and South Asia
Young graduates and back-office workers in AI-exposed services
Renters and first-time buyers in Anglo-sphere and Southern European cities
bullets: The world never had a single crisis, just a 2029 AI-capex bust and shallow US recession that pulled average growth down to ~2.6%.
Public debt crept past 100% of world GDP; G7 governments run persistent deficits and lean on central banks to cap long-end yields.
Trade has settled into three loose blocs with average tariffs higher than in 2026; India, the Gulf and ASEAN profit as connectors.
Five sovereign debt crises hit frontier economies, resolved slowly and partially, deepening Global South resentment of Western-led institutions.
AI is in a third of firms; cheaper post-bust compute spread it widely, but gains concentrate in capital owners and top earners.
Renewables reach ~42% of power, yet emissions merely plateau and warming of ~1.57C makes heat and crop shocks routine.
Trust in institutions has eroded further and protest over rents, food prices and jobs is more frequent but fragmented, not revolutionary.
A new Horn of Africa war and frozen conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East keep defence budgets and refugee flows high.
wildcard: A coordinated cyberattack briefly disabled a major cross-border payments messaging hub for 36 hours in 2030, accelerating the shift to bloc-specific payment rails.
image_description: On a sweltering evening in Nairobi, a laid-off call-centre worker sells phone repairs from a solar-powered kiosk beneath a billboard advertising AI tutors, while a queue forms at a subsidised maize depot across the street.
